# `assembly` commands

## `assembly build`

Build an inventory assembly from its bill of materials. Each component is consumed -- its quantity per assembly times `quantity` -- at its weighted-average cost on `date`, and the assembly is received at the sum; a non-stock component (service, non-inventory part, other charge) adds its purchase cost and credits its expense account, as the anchor does. A component that is itself an assembly is consumed from stock, never built automatically. Dry-run is the Build Assemblies window: each component with the quantity needed, on hand on the date and reserved by pending builds, and `max_buildable`, the most the components on hand allow. Building more is refused naming the shortages, unless `pending` is set: a pending build posts nothing, reserves its components and is built later with `assembly finalize`. The build posts as a journal entry the inventory ledger owns: debit the assembly's inventory asset account, credit each component's; where they share one account (the usual case) the general ledger does not move (`posts_to_ledger` false). Stock status, inventory valuation and the balance sheet agree on every date. A backdated build recosts later sales of its components and of the assembly by dated corrections, and a later backdated purchase of a component recosts the build and the assembly with it. A date in a closed period is refused.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | ledger.post |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/assembly.build` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow assembly build --item "Two-Valve Kit" --quantity 2 --date 2026-07-31 --reason "Built two kits today" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "assembly build", "input": {"item": "Two-Valve Kit", "quantity": "2", "date": "2026-07-31"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `item` | `--item` | string | yes | no | — | The inventory assembly item to build, by id or full name.; minimum length 1; maximum length 1000 |
| `quantity` | `--quantity` | string | yes | no | — | Quantity of the assembly to build, a positive decimal with at most six places.; minimum length 1; maximum length 40 |
| `date` | `--date` | string | yes | no | — | Build date: the components are consumed and the assembly received at their average cost on it.; minimum length 10; maximum length 10 |
| `memo` | `--memo` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Memo on the build. |
| `pending` | `--pending` | boolean | no | no | false | Mark the build pending when the components on hand are short of it: nothing is posted, the components are reserved, and `assembly finalize` builds it later. A build that can be built is built; pending applies only to a shortfall. |
| `site` | `--site` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Inventory site the components are taken from and the assembly put at, by id or name; omitted, the default site. |
| `bin` | `--bin` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Bin the built assemblies go into; omitted, its default bin at the site, else no bin. |
| `lot` | `--lot` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Lot the built assemblies receive into, when the assembly is lot-tracked. |
| `lot_expiry` | `--lot-expiry` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Expiry date of a new lot (ISO); change an existing lot's with `lot update`. |
| `serial_numbers` | `--serial-numbers` | array[string] \| null | no | yes | null | Serial numbers of the built units, when the assembly is serial-tracked; the rest are unassigned. |
| `components[].item` | inside `--components` JSON array | string | yes | no | — | Component item, by id or full name.; minimum length 1; maximum length 1000 |
| `components[].bin` | inside `--components` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | Bin the component is taken from; omitted, its default bin at the site, else no bin. |
| `components[].lot` | inside `--components` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | Lot the component is taken from. |
| `components[].serial_numbers` | inside `--components` JSON array | array[string] \| null | no | yes | null | Serial numbers of the component units taken. |

## `assembly delete`

Delete a build with a required reason. A pending build is removed and its components released; a posted build is voided first, exactly as `assembly void` does. The build drops off `assembly list`; its history stays readable with `assembly show` and `--status deleted`.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/assembly.delete` |

## `assembly finalize`

Build a pending build now that its components are on hand, on its own date or on `date`, from the bill of materials it reserved. Refused naming the shortages while they are still short.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |

## `assembly update`

Edit a build: its quantity, date or memo. A posted build is restated -- the old consumption and receipt are reversed exactly and the build is posted again at the average costs now, and later documents are recosted by dated corrections. A pending build stays pending. More than the components allow is refused; a closed period, old date or new, is refused.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | ledger.post |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/assembly.update` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow assembly update 01JASSEMBLYBUILD0000000001 --quantity 3 --reason "Three, not two" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "assembly update", "input": {"build": "01JASSEMBLYBUILD0000000001", "quantity": "3"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |

| `build` | `BUILD` | string | yes | no | — | The build, by its id or by the journal number it posted as.; minimum length 1; maximum length 1000 |
| `expected_version` | `--expected-version` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | The build version this edit was decided from; a later change is refused. |
| `quantity` | `--quantity` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Quantity of the assembly to build, a positive decimal with at most six places. Omitted, unchanged. |
| `date` | `--date` | string \| null | no | yes | null | New build date. Omitted, unchanged. |
| `memo` | `--memo` | string \| null | no | yes | null | New memo. Omitted, unchanged. |
| `site` | `--site` | string \| null | no | yes | null | New inventory site for the build. Omitted, unchanged. |

| `components[].cost.currency` | string | yes | no | — | — |

| `unit_cost` | object | yes | no | — | — |
| `unit_cost.amount` | string | yes | no | — | — |

| `warnings` | array[string] | no | no | [] | — |
| `history` | array[dict] | no | no | [] | Every revision of the build: version, status, date, quantity, who and when. |

## `assembly void`
